title: What If a Cartoon Made a Whole Country Want Pet Raccoons? Japan Found Out

scenes.text: What if a cartoon made a whole country want pet raccoons? Japan found out.
In 1977, an anime called Rascal the Raccoon ran for 52 episodes. Soon Japan was importing about 1,500 raccoons a year.
But a grown raccoon is aggressive and destructive. Owners gave up and, like the boy in the story, set them free.
By 2004, wild raccoons lived in 42 of Japan's 47 prefectures. By 2008, in all of them.
They raid crops, eat native frogs and salamanders, and nest in old temples. Hokkaido alone loses about 30 million yen a year.
Imports are banned now, and thousands are culled every year. One lovable character, one invasive species.

description:
What if a cartoon made a whole country want pet raccoons?
In 1977 the anime Rascal the Raccoon (Araiguma Rasukaru), based on Sterling North's 1963 memoir, ran for 52 episodes in Japan. Families began importing North American raccoons as pets, by most accounts up to about 1,500 a year. Adult raccoons proved aggressive and hard to keep, and many were released or escaped. A 2004 report found wild raccoons in at least 42 of Japan's 47 prefectures, and by 2008 they were in all 47. They damage crops (more than 30 million yen a year on Hokkaido alone), prey on native voles, frogs, crayfish and salamanders, and nest in the roofs of temples and shrines. Imports are now banned and thousands of raccoons are culled each year.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: In the story, the boy lets his raccoon go in the wild. Thousands of real owners did the same. Which other pet craze went wrong?
